summary: Facepalm: Facepalm scan for 2026-11-04 (window Oct. 29–Nov. 4). Most of what turned up was Election Day mishaps. One candidate fully meets the rules: on Nov. 3, Leavenworth County, Kan., ordered the wrong number of ballots for its Linwood polling place. The county's own .gov press release admits the ordering error and apologizes, and Fox News reports the Secretary of State's figures (1,000 needed, 100 received). I set the other leads aside because they had no blunder established, no second accepted source, or a cause that wasn't clear. The search budget ran out before I could find solid alternates. Genius: Scan for 2026-11-04 (GENIUS side; window Oct. 29 to Nov. 4). I'm submitting one candidate: the Golden State Valkyries' first WNBA title (Game 7, Oct. 31, San Francisco). It is backed by CBS News and NBC Bay Area, and I opened and checked both quotes on the live pages. The search budget ran out early, so I could not find second sources for the science leads or retry the swimming and marathon leads. The SF Chronicle and NPR pages returned 'url not allowed', the Phys.org pages were not accessible, and the Billings Gazette page is behind a TollBit paywall. Note that the 2026-11-03 genius story was also sports (Brewers), so this candidate does not add category variety. Pair published.

candidates.headline: Golden State Valkyries win the WNBA title in their second season, beating the Dream in Game 7
Leavenworth County, Kan., polling place gets 100 ballots instead of 1,000 after an ordering error
Chicago precincts run short of paper ballots on Election Day; elections board apologizes for a 'glitch'
candidates.reason: In the window (Nov. 3), with Sun-Times and ABC7 Chicago coverage, but the cause isn't established as a blunder. The board points to split precincts, and an Illinois State Board of Elections spokesman told Fox News that sending extra ballots when turnout runs high is not unusual.

candidates.headline: Brandywine, Md., polling place runs out of paper ballots on Election Day
candidates.reason: The cause isn't clear. WJLA/Fox Baltimore reports the site had no paper ballots, while Fox News, citing The Banner, says it had the wrong ballots. No blunder by officials is clearly established.

candidates.headline: Knott County, Ky., officials cite 'human error' for a lack of ballots at polling sites
candidates.reason: In the window (Nov. 3), but the only coverage found was WYMT, which isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Election error gives some Bismarck, N.D., voters the wrong ballot
candidates.reason: In the window (Nov. 3), but the only coverage found was North Dakota Monitor, Valley News Live, KFYR and Yahoo, none of which is accepted.

candidates.headline: Piscataway, N.J., school polling site locked at the start of voting after confusion over security guards
candidates.reason: A brief delay of about 15 minutes in which no one was turned away, and the only copy found was a Yahoo republication (banned). No accepted source was opened.

candidates.headline: North Carolina extends voting hours at five precincts in four counties
candidates.reason: Officials attribute the extensions to computer issues at polling sites, which is an equipment problem, not an established blunder.

candidates.headline: Pulaski County, Ark., bureaucracy failed to catch a reported $1.9 million email scam
candidates.reason: The county was the victim of a crime (email fraud), which the rules exclude.

candidates.headline: Massachusetts resident accidentally gives out laxatives during trick-or-treat
candidates.reason: The people affected are children who may have been harmed, which the rules exclude.

candidates.headline: Zouhair Talbi runs the fastest NYC Marathon ever by an American man (Nov. 1)
candidates.reason: Still only one accepted source. The NPR race story returned 'url not allowed', and the other coverage found (LetsRun, FloTrack, World-Track, Track & Field News, Suunto) is not accepted. The search limit ran out before ABC7 New York or AP could be found again.

candidates.headline: Jack Alexy sets short-course 100m freestyle world record (44.64) in Westmont, Ill. (Oct. 30)
candidates.reason: Still only one accepted source (Fox News/OutKick). Searches for NJ.com and North Jersey coverage returned only Yahoo, NBC Sports, SwimSwam and Swimming World, none of which is accepted.

candidates.headline: Katharine Berkoff sets short-course 50m backstroke world record in Westmont, Ill. (Oct. 29)
candidates.reason: Billings Gazette's page is still blocked by a TollBit paywall. The other coverage (Montana Sports, Missoula Current, Ravalli Republic) is not accepted.

candidates.headline: Hawkmoths repeatedly evolved genital ultrasound to jam bat sonar (Science News, Nov. 3)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source. The other coverage (ScienceAlert, Yahoo, Archyde) is not accepted, and the article body didn't load, so I couldn't confirm which institutions ran the study or when the paper was published.

candidates.headline: Cancer cells' own carbon monoxide used to make anticancer drugs inside them (Nature Communications)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The research is from RIKEN in Japan. It is also an early laboratory study.

candidates.headline: Possible red blood cells found in a 115-million-year-old dinosaur fossil (CNN, Nov. 3)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The study is from Curtin University in Australia, and CNN notes that not every scientist is convinced.

candidates.headline: Voyager 1 nears one light-day from Earth
candidates.reason: It hasn't happened yet. ScienceDaily says the milestone is still to come, so there is nothing to report inside the window.

candidates.headline: Pulsars set first mass limits on supermassive black hole pairs; physicists near the 'Zeptoverse' after a 42-year particle search (Phys.org, Nov. 3–4)
candidates.reason: The Phys.org pages were not accessible, so I couldn't confirm the institutions or whether the work was done in the US. The search limit ran out before any second source turned up.

candidates.headline: Hidden companion star Siwarha disturbing Betelgeuse's atmosphere (ScienceDaily, Nov. 3)
candidates.reason: The ScienceDaily page was not accessible, so I couldn't confirm the institutions or the publication date, and there is no second source. The finding is also hedged ('new evidence suggests').
